result:
The proposed answer of 2 is incorrect, because the argument wrongly treats every non-extreme character as contributing nothing in the limit.

Take λ = (n−1,1). Here χ(σ) = fix(σ) − 1 and χ(1) = n−1. For A_n and B_n, fix = ⌊H√n⌋, so χ(A_n) ≈ χ(B_n) ≈ H√n. For C_n, which has no fixed points, χ(C_n) = −1. The contribution of this character is therefore

(H√n)²·(−1)/(n−1) → −H².

This does not vanish, and it depends on H. The same holds for its sign-twist, (2,1^{n−2}), because the product of signs is 1. So the claimed bound |χ(σ)|/χ(1) ≤ χ(1)^{−δ} cannot control the product of the three characters here. The fixed points of A_n and B_n make the near-trivial characters contribute at order 1.

More generally, the partitions (n−k, μ) with |μ| = k contribute at order H^{2k}, in a Poisson-like pattern. I did not derive the full sum, but this pattern points to a limit of the form 2e^{−H²} rather than 2. That would match 2 only when H = 0, which the problem excludes since H > 0.

The final answer of 2 is therefore wrong.

VERDICT: REJECT
